proposal.distinction: The refinement separates defined fund status, the kind of change and the regulator's selected control. A UCITS domiciled outside the enumerated jurisdictions is outside scope, rather than a failed in-scope eligibility case. A supervised operator change also does not become a material investment change merely because both receive streamlining. The tested rival would make introductory home supervision an additional item (ii) condition: it could exclude an otherwise home-compliant change lacking such supervision. That rival has some support in the introduction, but 'aim at' and the express supervision language in item (i), contrasted with item (ii)'s compliance language, do not establish a second executable condition. The strongest remaining uncertainty is whether the pending-application transition preserves substantive requirements. No comparable fact-bound counterexample was supplied; incomparability diagnostics do not establish disagreement on a shared case.

Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.

proposal.distinction: The text supports a clear removal-of-approval eligibility rule for changes outside the transition, rather than rival conjunctive and disjunctive exception rules. For example, an ordinary home-compliant investment-policy change in a covered Irish UCITS after the Effective Date qualifies if it has no possible local policy implications; the same change with possible local policy implications does not qualify even if it is neither novel nor complex. For an otherwise identical application received on 27 November 2025 and pending at transition, existing processing applies and this formal control gives no answer. The strongest uncertainty is whether that preserved processing also necessarily preserves the substantive approval prerequisite.

proposal.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Within scope, true means the identified change qualifies for this circular’s removal of the SFC prior-approval requirement on the assessment date. False means at least one removal condition fails, including the application transition; it does not by itself establish that prior approval is required. Unknown facts remain unknown. This is a proposed eligibility interpretation, not legal approval.
proposal.subject: Eligibility for removal of prior SFC approval for a material UCITS investment change

assumptions: This models only eligibility for the circular's stated approval relief, subject to unavailable operational authorities.
The specific Effective Date governs the introductory immediate-effect language.
An application received before the Effective Date and unapproved at that date preserves the existing process and blocks use of this relief for the selected application.
Novelty, complexity and possible local policy implications independently defeat item (ii) relief.
The purpose statement does not add a separate home-supervision test to item (ii).
The identified change is assessed as a whole; no severability or withdrawal rule is inferred.

citations.quote: Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.

proposal.distinction: Retains the parent's practical attachment of the transition to relief eligibility. Otherwise identical qualifying changes can receive different results because one has a preserved application. The strongest uncertainty is that the transition expressly addresses processing, while the additional substantive exclusion is an inference.
